meta.move: Mixed: good evidence, then raises Claire
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste it, Hale. Owen found out about his zero from his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided on that zero, and was Owen heard before it went in?
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. Was Owen heard before it went in, and on what basis was it entered?
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.
I'm writing that line down. A misquoted line is a citation problem, not a zero. What else do you have?
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.

You'll want to be very careful about the next sentence, Hale. Claire won her appeal, and you just said "it seems to run in the family" about my son, which I'm writing down word for word. When we're done here, I'm walking that sentence straight into the principal's office.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require that Owen's zero be withdrawn, that nothing about this goes on his record, and an apology for how he learned of it and for what was said about my family. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, still demanding the zero be withdrawn and agreeing to nothing.
What moved her: "I should have called you before entering the zero" because a plain one-sentence ownership of the process earned her only small sign of ground.
What cost ground: "It seems to run in the family" because bringing up her daughter's old case turned her cold and sent her toward the principal.
Try next time: after the misquoted line, when she asked what else you had, show her a dated document tied to Owen's own work on the essay and leave Claire out of it entirely.
